title: Etale cohomology of a finite coproduct of geometric points
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $I$ be a finite set, and let $C=\coprod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the finite coproduct of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. For an abelian etale sheaf $F$ on $C_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], choose the geometric point $\bar c_i$ on the $i$-th summand, with geometric stalk $F_{\bar c_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Then the etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] satisfies $H^q(C,F)=0$ for every $q>0$, and the canonical map $H^0(C,F)\to\prod_{i\in I}F_{\bar c_i}$ is an isomorphism (the product is finite).

source.place: Theorem 03QT (etale-cohomology-theorem-equivalence-sheaves-point) and Lemma 03QU (etale-cohomology-lemma-compare-cohomology-point), Section 03QQ (section-cohomology-point), applied componentwise to the finite disjoint union; the finite-product assembly is the first paragraph of the proof of Lemma 0A5B (etale-cohomology-lemma-constant-smooth-statements)

proof.text: For each summand $C_i=\operatorname{Spec}k$, restrict $F$ to the etale site of $C_i$. The single-point calculation [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-cohomology], obtained from the equivalence of etale sheaves with sets on a separably closed point and the comparison of sections with the geometric stalk, gives $H^q(C_i,F|_{C_i})=0$ for $q>0$ and identifies $H^0(C_i,F|_{C_i})$ with $F_{\bar c_i}$.

The etale site of the finite disjoint union is the finite product of the etale sites of its open-and-closed summands. Consequently the global-sections functor is the finite product of the component global-sections functors, and its derived functors are the corresponding finite products. The geometric stalk of $F|_{C_i}=\iota_i^{-1}F$ at $\bar c_i$ is identified with the stalk $F_{\bar c_i}$ of $F$ at the image geometric point by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] applied to the inclusion $\iota_i:C_i\to C$. Using Step 1 componentwise gives $H^q(C,F)=0$ for $q>0$ and the canonical isomorphism $H^0(C,F)\cong\prod_{i\in I}F_{\bar c_i}$; the product is finite.
